story: Saturday night in Sumter Oaks is warm at 80 degrees, and it's Halloween, so the Rec Center is emptying out as Gary and Donna head down to Magnolia Loop to see the trick-or-treaters. Hal stays on Magnolia Loop and tells Rosa, in his own gruff way, that her dinner was good, then agrees to coffee tomorrow on the condition that he brings his own mug. Rosa heads off toward Town Square, leaving Hal looking mildly pleased with himself as the golf carts hum past.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Our two hours on court one are done and we both said we were heading to the Loop. Donna's still beside me, so I should stop talking and actually go. The parade's winding down, cider's waiting at Rosa's, and I still need to check in on my cart application. Time to get moving to Magnolia Loop.

parameters.content: Heading out to the Loop to catch the tail end of the parade and meet Donna at Rosa's for cider.

donna.thought_process: Gary has said goodbye twice now and is heading to the Loop, so there's nothing more to say here. I promised Hal I'd hide the extra flamingos behind the hedge before parade day, and the courts are handed back after our two hours. Time to head out to Magnolia Loop, tidy the ornaments, then catch up with Gary for cider and the costume contest sign-up.

parameters.content: Heading out to the Loop to hide those extra flamingos, then I'll find Gary for cider and the costume contest.

hal.thought_process: Rosa is right in front of me and just thanked me for coming to dinner, so a gruff but warm reply is in order. I haven't answered her yet, and a sergeant returns courtesy. Donna promised to thin the flock after her drills, and I've been told to come count myself, so the flamingo flock can wait until she's had her chance. The notebook stays in my pocket tonight, since the parade was lively and the street looks orderly enough. Coffee on her porch tomorrow sounds fine, and I'll say so without making a fuss about being soft-hearted.

parameters.content: Dinner was good, Rosa, and I'll say so out loud once. I'll take you up on that coffee tomorrow, and I'll bring my own mug, since I don't trust anyone's measurements but my own.

rosa.thought_process: I've already thanked Hal and invited him to the contest and coffee, so asking again would just be nagging. He's busy counting flamingos with his notebook anyway. The dinner went well, the neighbors are happy, and my goal of getting everyone to one table is done. It's late, the contest is on at the Square, and I've got a note up on the bulletin board already. I'll head to the Town Square to catch the cart judging and enjoy the evening instead of rushing around.

parameters.content: Heading to the costume contest to see the decorated carts and cheer on the neighbors

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
